articles.title: India's Pay Raises Are Widening the Gap Between Formal and Informal Workers
articles.excerpt: Informal wages rose just 3.88% to ₹1,46,550 a year in 2024-25 while formal pay grew 9.2%, leaving 88% of informal workers below the ₹17,498 monthly benchmark, ASUSE and PLFS data show.
articles.nri_angle: The formal-informal wage split shapes the remittance and family-support economics of millions of households with members working abroad, and the job quality awaiting returnees.

articles.title: FSSAI Proposes Ban on Added Sugars in Infant Food for Babies Under Six Months
articles.excerpt: A draft amendment published on October 16 would bar adding sucrose and fructose to products for infants up to six months, with 60 days for public comment before the rules can be finalised.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora parents who buy Indian-made infant food should note the ban is still a draft — sucrose and fructose remain permitted within limits until final rules are notified, so ingredient lists are the check that matters today.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi's AQI Leaps From 65 to 216 in a Day as Calm Weather Traps Pollution
articles.excerpt: Friday's rain briefly gave the capital satisfactory air. With the IMD forecasting dry, still days ahead, the winter pollution season has arrived early — and GRAP Stage 1 is already in force.
articles.image_caption: South Block is engulfed in a layer of smog in New Delhi. Delhi's AQI jumped from 65 to 216 in a day as dry, calm weather trapped pollutants over the capital.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families flying into Delhi for Diwali face AQI swings from 65 to 216 within a day; morning AQI checks and masks for sensitive travellers are now part of the trip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: LK Advani, 98, Admitted to Delhi Hospital With Chest Infection, Condition Stable
articles.excerpt: The former deputy prime minister was brought to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Friday evening and is under observation in the pulmonary department. It is his third hospital admission in under two years.
articles.image_caption: L. K. Advani, the former deputy prime minister and BJP founding figure admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Delhi with a chest infection.
articles.nri_angle: Advani is a towering figure for a generation of Indians at home and abroad who followed the BJP's rise; his health is followed closely across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Dead, Six Injured as Reactor Blast Rocks Bharuch Pharma Plant in Gujarat
articles.excerpt: A reactor failed during a hydrogenation process at a pharmaceutical unit in the Saykha GIDC area of Vagra, leaking methylene dichloride gas. Officials have opened an investigation and no cause has been established.
articles.image_caption: An injured person is loaded into an ambulance at night while medical staff and bystanders assist. The reactor blast at the Bharuch pharmaceutical plant killed five people and injured six, according to India Today.
articles.nri_angle: Bharuch's chemical belt is a major employer for Gujarati families in India and a region many in the diaspora come from; recurring fatal plant accidents there are a standing safety concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 24 Indian Seafarers Safe After Tankers Hit in Hormuz and Off Romania, Minister Says
articles.excerpt: Crude tanker MT ST 3, with 15 Indian crew, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 16; chemical tanker Yara J, with nine Indians aboard, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage on October 14. No casualties on either vessel.
articles.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's merchant crews; every attack on commercial shipping in the Gulf or Black Sea puts Indian families on shore on alert.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Marches to Supreme Court, Demands Election Chief's Resignation Over Voter Rolls
articles.excerpt: Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi led thousands toward the Supreme Court on Monday; stopped 600 metres short, opposition leaders filed a petition against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the voter-roll revision.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi. INDIA bloc parties marched to the court demanding the Election Chief's resignation over voter rolls.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs remain enrolled as overseas electors and have family members among those struck from the rolls; re-enrolment is open through the Election Commission's voter portal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Blackouts Hit Indian Factories as Coal Crunch Squeezes the Economy
articles.excerpt: Punjab factories face unscheduled 3–4 hour power cuts as coal stocks hit their lowest since 2021 — but the government says depletion has slowed sharply in October and supplies are stabilizing.
articles.image_caption: Coal-laden open wagons stand in an Indian railway yard, part of the freight network that carries coal from mines to power plants. The Ministry of Coal says higher rake loading — 469 rakes a day in early October, up about 10% from September — is slowing the depletion of plant stockpiles.
articles.nri_angle: The blackouts affect NRI families in Punjab directly, and the coal crunch is a national growth risk for diaspora investors watching India's economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Names Modi, Shah Over Delhi Protest Crackdown, Calls Supreme Court March
articles.excerpt: The Congress leader accused police and BJP workers of beating peaceful protesters, announced a Monday march to the Supreme Court over voter-roll revision — and the BJP hit straight back.
articles.image_caption: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing supporters
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the Delhi crackdown and the SIR fight are becoming the touchstone case in how India's democratic health is read abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Naga Council Issues 48-Hour Ultimatum Over Severed Head as Manipur Clashes Kill Nine
articles.excerpt: The Joint Tribes Council Manipur demands the return of Ajinbou R's severed head within 48 hours after a weekend of Kuki-Naga clashes killed nine people across three hill districts.
articles.image_caption: Security personnel patrol a road in Manipur's hill districts as smoke rises in the distance. The Naga Council has issued a 48-hour ultimatum demanding the return of a Naga man's severed head after fresh clashes killed nine people.
articles.nri_angle: The fresh Kuki-Naga clashes are the latest rupture in Manipur's hill districts for a diaspora that watches each flare-up for signs of a wider conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Roorkee Graduate Builds His Own Prosthetic Leg, Targets 2028 Paralympics
articles.excerpt: Amputee engineer Saurav Kumar designed his own prosthetic, co-founded a deep-tech startup, and is swimming for India — with Paralympic gold in his sights.
articles.image_caption: An athlete with a prosthetic leg on a running track. The IIT Roorkee graduate built his own prosthetic leg and is targeting the 2028 Paralympics.
articles.nri_angle: A scholarship-and-loan-funded IIT graduate who built his own prosthetic and chases Paralympic gold — the rare story that speaks to both NRI faith in Indian education and the disability-rights causes the diaspora funds back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After a 12.6% Monsoon Shortfall, India's Reservoirs Run Low as Super El Niño Looms
articles.excerpt: The weakest monsoon in eleven years has left reservoirs below average and drought declarations in three states — with a super El Niño set to peak in December.
articles.nri_angle: A weak monsoon plus super El Niño threatens food inflation and water rationing in India — directly affecting remittance-receiving rural families and the consumption story NRI investors hold in Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Agricultural GVA growth projected at 1.6% in FY27.
Rural economy expected to slow through 2026 and 2027.

articles.title: CPI(M) MP John Brittas Dragged and Assaulted by Delhi Police, Then Dumped Roadside
articles.excerpt: The Rajya Sabha MP says he was manhandled inside a police bus despite identifying himself as a parliamentarian, released only after a DCP reviewed body-cam footage; he has written to the President and CJI seeking an independent investigation.
articles.image_caption: Security personnel restrain CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas in New Delhi on October 11, 2026. Brittas alleges he was dragged from a press interaction and assaulted inside a police vehicle during the protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.nri_angle: The incident tests the Supreme Court's just-issued limits on protest policing in India and has become a reference point for how dissent and democratic rights are handled in the world's largest democracy — a live question for the global diaspora watching Indian institutions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amritsar-Born Diplomat Tells Pakistan at UN: India Will Not Bow to Nuclear Blackmail
articles.excerpt: Anmol Sher Singh Bedi, Senior Adviser (Disarmament) at India's Geneva mission, exercised India's right of reply at the UNGA First Committee, rejecting Pakistan's Kashmir claims and setting three red lines on terror and nuclear rhetoric.
articles.image_caption: A turbaned Indian diplomat speaks at the India desk during a United Nations session. Anmol Sher Singh Bedi delivered India's right of reply to Pakistan at the UNGA First Committee meeting on disarmament and international security.
articles.nri_angle: India's UN posture during UNGA season resonates strongly with the global diaspora, and Bedi's three-red-line framework — fitting response to terror, no sponsor-mastermind distinction, rejection of nuclear blackmail — signals how India would respond to any future terror incident affecting Indian interests abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Muslim Artisans Weave Durga's Hair: West Bengal's Story of Harmony
articles.excerpt: In Howrah's Parbatipur village, Muslim artisans have woven Maa Durga's wavy hair for generations — but rising jute prices and a changing social climate are fraying the trade.
articles.image_caption: Artisans in West Bengal craft the hair of Goddess Durga.
articles.nri_angle: A quiet story of Muslim-Hindu craftsmanship behind Durga Puja that diaspora readers will rarely see — and a concrete way US puja committees can support the artisans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Condemns 'Deeply Concerning' Attacks on Two Indian-Crewed Tankers in Gulf of Oman
articles.excerpt: The MEA's Sunday statement confirmed MT Petro Dolphin's drone strike at Sohar Anchorage — nine of 11 Indian crew safe, two missing — and a projectile strike on MT Valthera, whose 11 Indian seafarers are safe, while urging de-escalation.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker underway (file photo) — India condemned attacks on two Indian-crewed tankers in the Gulf of Oman on October 11 (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India is one of the world's largest suppliers of merchant navy crews, so attacks on Indian-crewed Gulf shipping are a direct threat to a major diaspora livelihood; the MEA's condemnation and the Muscat embassy's family-facing coordination are the operative channels for affected families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Indian Dead, Three in ICU After Riyadh Airport Attack; Embassy Issues Stay-Indoors Advisory
articles.excerpt: Mohammad Yousuf Ali, a 46-year-old Umrah pilgrim from Hyderabad, died of his injuries while three injured Indians remain in intensive care but stable; the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has told nationals to stay alert and indoors as necessary.
articles.image_caption: An Indian embassy official visits an injured Indian national in a Riyadh hospital. Embassy officials have visited every hospital where Indians injured in the King Khalid International Airport attack are admitted.
articles.nri_angle: The attack directly threatens one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities, with the embassy's stay-indoors advisory, casualty support and repatriation help applying to Indians working, studying or performing Umrah in Saudi Arabia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PM Modi Flags Off Chennai Metro Phase 2, Cutting Poonamallee–Vadapalani Trip to 30 Minutes
articles.excerpt: The 14.6-km Yellow Line section — Phase 2's first operational stretch — connects the western suburbs to the metro network with fares from ₹10 and peak trains every 10 minutes.
articles.image_caption: A Chennai Metro train (file photo) — PM Modi and Tamil Nadu CM Vijay inaugurated the Poonamallee Bypass–Vadapalani stretch of Phase 2 on October 11, cutting the trip to about 30 minutes.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs arriving in Chennai get a fast, cheap new rail link to the western suburbs and industrial belt, with direct interchange to the airport and Central station.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 11-Day Mysuru Dasara Begins With Traditional Inauguration at Chamundi Hills
articles.excerpt: Karnataka's state festival runs October 11-21, culminating in the golden-howdah Jamboo Savari procession on Vijayadashami.
articles.image_caption: A decorated elephant carries the golden howdah during the Jamboo Savari procession in Mysuru. The 2026 Mysuru Dasara festivities began October 11 and run through Vijayadashami on October 21.
articles.nri_angle: Dasara week is prime festive-season travel time for NRIs: the illuminated Mysuru Palace and the Jamboo Savari procession make October 11-21 the best window to visit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Released CJP Leaders Vow Nationwide Protests, Escalating Standoff Over Voter Roll Revision
articles.excerpt: Hours after a Delhi court released three CJP conveners from preventive custody, the group promised to take its demand for the Election Commission chief's resignation across the country — setting up a fresh confrontation with authorities.
articles.image_caption: Protesters in New Delhi. Released CJP leaders vowed nationwide protests until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns over the voter-roll revision.
articles.nri_angle: The sharpest flashpoint yet in the opposition's months-long campaign against the Election Commission's voter-roll revision — with practical implications for anyone travelling to Delhi this week.

articles.title: Assam-Born Scientist Builds Detectors for NASA Telescope That Will Hunt for Life Beyond Earth
articles.excerpt: Dr. Angaraj Duara is developing CMOS image detectors at the Open University for potential use on NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory, the first large telescope designed to search for life on other worlds.
articles.image_caption: A NASA telescope that will hunt for signs of life on distant exoplanets. An Assam-born scientist built its detectors.
articles.nri_angle: Duara's trajectory — Assam to Leicester to a NASA flagship mission with UK Space Agency funding — is a working blueprint for Indian STEM talent abroad, and his public lectures carry the science back to India as well.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Bars Illegal Detentions, Orders Normal Metro and Internet in Delhi Protest Case
articles.excerpt: A special Sunday bench barred illegal detention of peaceful protesters and ordered normal metro, rail and internet services after petitions alleged a crackdown on the October 10 anti-CEC protest.
articles.image_caption: A Rapid Action Force officer stands atop a police vehicle fitted with a tear-gas shell launcher during a security deployment in Delhi. The Supreme Court on Sunday barred the illegal detention of peaceful protesters and ordered normal metro, rail and internet services following the October 10 protest crackdown.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs following India's democratic institutions, the Supreme Court's weekend intervention is a significant signal about judicial oversight of protest policing — the CJI, whom the court protects, is also receiving the opposition's October 12 memorandum on the vote-chori allegations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc to March in Delhi on October 12, Submit Memorandum to Chief Justice
articles.excerpt: A day after meeting President Murmu to demand the CEC's resignation, opposition leaders announced a Delhi march and a memorandum to CJI Surya Kant, with Congress ordering all MPs to stay in the capital.
articles.image_caption: Opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Mamata Banerjee gather in New Delhi. The INDIA bloc will march through the capital on October 12 and submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant.
articles.nri_angle: The diaspora follows electoral-integrity debates in India closely as a measure of its democratic standing, and the SIR roll revision at the heart of the row affects emigrant families with relatives on the rolls.

articles.title: IAF chief tells US general: no official F-35 offer, India still waiting
articles.excerpt: At the close of Exercise Tarang Shakti-2026 in Jodhpur, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh said Washington has never formally offered the F-35 — while Russia's Su-57 pitch also awaits a decision.
articles.image_caption: F-35 fighter jets of the U.S. Air Force parked at an air base. Representative image.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-Americans follow US-India defence ties closely; India's refusal to let F-35 rhetoric become policy shows New Delhi negotiating with Washington from a position of deliberate caution.
